title: How clan membership worked in practice
body_text: In historical Scotland, clan membership was shaped as much by residence and allegiance as by ancestry. People could become associated with a clan through protection, service, marriage, or long-term settlement. Loyalty and mutual obligation mattered more than fixed surnames. This flexibility allowed clans to adapt to political and social change.
